hotels.name: Ginza Lantern Hotel

hotels.name: Arashiyama River Retreat
hotels.description: Riverside retreat at the edge of the bamboo grove, with an open-air bath and bicycles to borrow.

hotels.name: Higashiyama Machiya Suites

hotels.name: Umeda Skyline Suites

itinerary.title: Arrive in Tokyo, ease in around Asakusa
itinerary.summary: Land, check in and keep the first day light — one anchor sight plus an easy dinner near your hotel.

activities.name: Sensō-ji Temple, Asakusa
activities.description: Tokyo’s oldest temple, reached through the lantern-lined Nakamise shopping street. Go before 8am for empty photographs.

activities.name: Akihabara Electric Town
activities.description: Six-floor arcades, gachapon halls and vintage anime figure shops. Best after 11am when the stores open.

activities.name: Omoide Yokocho & Golden Gai, Shinjuku
activities.description: Two warrens of six-seat bars and yakitori counters. Cover charges are normal (¥500–1,000) — ask before sitting.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

itinerary.notes: Dinner: Omoide Yokocho & Golden Gai, Shinjuku — Shinjuku. Rain likely: indoor alternatives prioritised. Airport transfer is included in your transport budget.

itinerary.title: Toyosu & Tsukiji — teamLab Planets digital art museum
itinerary.summary: teamLab Planets digital art museum → Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast crawl → Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden. Grouped to keep travel under 20 minutes between stops.

activities.name: teamLab Planets digital art museum
activities.description: Barefoot, immersive light rooms you walk through. Timed tickets sell out; bare legs are required for the water rooms.

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast crawl
activities.description: Six alleys of tamagoyaki, uni, grilled scallops and knife shops. Arrive by 8am — by 11am the best stalls close.

activities.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
activities.description: Three garden styles in one park — Japanese pond, English lawn, French parterre. Cherry blossoms peak late March.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

itinerary.title: Shibuya & Harajuku — Shibuya Scramble Crossing & Shibuya Sky
itinerary.summary: Shibuya Scramble Crossing & Shibuya Sky → Meiji Jingū Shrine & Yoyogi Park. Grouped to keep travel under 20 minutes between stops.

activities.name: Shibuya Scramble Crossing & Shibuya Sky
activities.description: The world’s busiest crossing, best seen from above at Shibuya Sky around sunset. Book the rooftop slot online a week ahead.

activities.name: Meiji Jingū Shrine & Yoyogi Park
activities.description: A cedar forest in the middle of the city, with a calm shrine courtyard. Combine with Harajuku’s Takeshita Street next door.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

itinerary.title: Higashiyama & Gion — Kiyomizu-dera & Sannenzaka lanes
itinerary.summary: First full day in Kyoto: Kiyomizu-dera & Sannenzaka lanes → Machiya tea ceremony in a 100-year-old townhouse.

activities.name: Kiyomizu-dera & Sannenzaka lanes
activities.description: Wooden stage above a hillside of maples, with stone lanes of pottery shops leading down to Gion.

activities.name: Machiya tea ceremony in a 100-year-old townhouse
activities.description: A 60-minute whisked-matcha ceremony with a host explaining the etiquette. Small groups of 6–8.

activities.name: Nishiki Market food walk
activities.description: A 400-metre covered market of pickles, tamagoyaki, yuba and matcha sweets. Eat standing, then move on.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

itinerary.notes: Dinner: Nishiki Market food walk — Nakagyo. Rain likely: indoor alternatives prioritised.

itinerary.title: Fushimi & Gion — Fushimi Inari Taisha
itinerary.summary: Fushimi Inari Taisha → Gion & Shirakawa canal at dusk → Philosopher’s Path to Ginkaku-ji. Grouped to keep travel under 20 minutes between stops.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
activities.description: Thousands of vermilion torii gates climbing Mount Inari. Walk 30 minutes past the crowd for empty gates.

activities.name: Gion & Shirakawa canal at dusk
activities.description: Willow-lined canal, teahouses and lantern light. Best 30 minutes before sunset, then dinner in Pontochō.

activities.name: Philosopher’s Path to Ginkaku-ji
activities.description: A canal-side stone path lined with cherry trees and small cafés, ending at the silver pavilion.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

itinerary.title: Chuo & Nipponbashi — Osaka Castle & park
itinerary.summary: First full day in Osaka: Osaka Castle & park → Kuromon Ichiba Market.

activities.name: Osaka Castle & park
activities.description: Reconstructed keep with a museum of the 1615 siege, surrounded by moats and cherry trees.

activities.name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
activities.description: 580 metres of uni, wagyu skewers, fugu and fruit. A 90-minute graze that replaces lunch.

activities.name: Shinsekai & kushikatsu lane
activities.description: Retro 1912 district under Tsūtenkaku tower. The rule at kushikatsu counters: never double-dip the sauce.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

itinerary.notes: Dinner: Shinsekai & kushikatsu lane — Shinsekai. Rain likely: indoor alternatives prioritised.

itinerary.title: Final morning in Osaka & departure
itinerary.summary: Umeda Sky Building Floating Garden → Nakanoshima river walk & National Museum of Art. Grouped to keep travel under 20 minutes between stops.

activities.name: Umeda Sky Building Floating Garden
activities.description: Two towers joined by a rooftop ring 173m up. Arrive 40 minutes before sunset for the full transition.

activities.name: Nakanoshima river walk & National Museum of Art
activities.description: A quiet river island of brick warehouses, a modern art museum and waterside coffee.

weather.summary: Mixed, carry a light rain jacket

sources.label: Visa & entry
sources.detail: Indians need a visa for Japan. Apply at VFS Global 4–6 weeks ahead with itinerary, bank statements and hotel bookings. A visa is required even for short tourism stays.

sources.label: Safety snapshot
sources.detail: very safe — Tokyo is one of the safest large cities in the world. Violent crime is rare; the practical risks are earthquakes, summer heatstroke and getting lost in station complexes.

activities.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary, Ubud
activities.description: Mossy banyan temple grounds with 1,200 long-tailed macaques and three 14th-century temples.

activities.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
activities.description: Stepped emerald terraces with swing platforms and jungle cafes. Arrive by 07:30 before the tour buses.

itinerary.summary: Mount Batur sunrise trek. Grouped to keep travel under 20 minutes between stops.

activities.name: Mount Batur sunrise trek
activities.description: 2am pick-up, 2-hour pre-dawn climb, sunrise above a volcanic caldera. Moderate fitness required.

itinerary.title: Nusa Penida — Nusa Penida day trip (Kelingking Beach)
itinerary.summary: Nusa Penida day trip (Kelingking Beach). Grouped to keep travel under 20 minutes between stops.

activities.name: Nusa Penida day trip (Kelingking Beach)

activities.name: Uluwatu Temple & Kecak fire dance

activities.name: Lake Pichola sunset boat & Jag Mandir
